text:
support-ops: FYI multiple customers reporting 503s across eu-west & us-west starting ~09:12 UTC after deployment. Error spike from 0.4% -> ~12%.
support-ops: initial logs attached, looks like upstream inference worker crashes (SIGSEGV) and GPU OOMs interleaved.
julia: oncall, can we get eyes and decide rollback vs mitigation? :eyes:
oncall-bot: paging @samir (oncall)
samir: looking now. pulling recent worker logs and nvml stats.
samir: quick sample from a crashed worker:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:34.891Z infer-runner[pid=14322]: KV_PREFETCH: prefetching 81920 tokens
2026-03-17T09:12:34.932Z infer-runner[pid=14322]: GPU_MEM_USAGE: 12.3GB/12.8GB
2026-03-17T09:12:34.945Z infer-runner[pid=14322]: *** caught SIGSEGV at 0x7f8c... ***
2026-03-17T09:12:35.002Z kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 14322 (infer-runner)
```
samir: pattern: large context prefetch + aggressive batching -> transient mem spike -> segfault/oom in runtime. Seen on 3 hosts in hosted-prod pool.
infra-eng: is this model-specific or request-shape specific?
support-ops: customers call out two models: redwood-open-7b-qlora and open-16b-std. All crashes correlate with requests that include long system+user context + batch resizing.
kernelflow: GPU telemetry shows memory climbs to >97% then NV driver resets on two GPUs, correlated with worker PID restarts.
eng-sre: immediate mitigations: (1) route new requests to fallback pool (dedicated smaller models), (2) disable kv-prefetch for hosted pool, (3) throttle large-context requests at gateway. Which is fastest?
samir: I can flip kv-prefetch flag off for hosted pool in ~2m and push a canary hotfix to 20% capacity. That should stop the prefetch memory surge.
julia: please also spin up fallback routing for active customers hitting 503s. customer-liaison: can you notify affected accounts with short ETA?
customer-liaison: pinged top 6 affected accounts, told them we're applying a hotfix and will update in 30m. asked for any repro payloads.
infra-eng: command to flip route (example):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routing/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"selector":{"pool":"hosted-prod"},"action":"route_to_dedicated","percentage":100}'
```
oncall-bot: samir started hotfix deployment to hosted-prod canary (20%).
samir: hotfix = disable kv_prefetch + enforce max_batch_tokens=4096 for hosted runtime. Applying now.
kernelflow: after hotfix on canary: crash rate down from 11% -> 0.6% in that subset. memory spikes no longer hit NV threshold.
eng-sre: good. start progressive ramp to 100% if stable for 10m and monitor.
samir: rolling to 100% now. leaving prefetch off until we have a safe prefetch window.
infra-eng: also initiated a controlled rollback option if we see other regressions.
support-ops: opened ticket PROD-4582 with logs, affected customer list, and repro steps.
samir: repro notes for the postmortem (saved to PROD-4582):
- send requests with > 32k total context across batch
- include system prompt with large embeddings + simultaneous batch resize
- run against hosted-prod runtime image v2026.03.17-rc2
Example cURL:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b-qlora","inputs":[{"prompt":"<very long context...>","max_tokens":512}],"batching":{"target_tokens":81920}}'
```
kernelflow: follow-up: one remaining host showed an OOM-kill instead of segfault after the hotfix; that host had stale driver (nvml v12.1 vs 12.3). infra-eng: isolating and reprovisioning that node.
eng-sre: action items assigned:
- samir: PR to add safety guardrails (reject >64k combined tokens at gateway) + runtime limit flags. (ETA 48h)
- infra-eng: add nvml driver mismatch alert and auto-drain for mismatched hosts. (ETA 72h)
- support-ops: update customer comms & add KB with temporary mitigations. (ETA 2h)
- qa: add regression test that simulates high-context prefetch concurrency across batches.
julia: thanks team. final status: hotfix rolled to 100%, crash rate back to baseline ~0.2%, affected customers rerouted or notified.
customer-liaison: sending second status update now, ETA for full follow-up postmortem ~48h.
support-ops: closing incident thread for now, will reopen if we see new spikes. :thumbsup:
__notes: Generated Slack thread about hosted inference worker crashes causing 503s; follows agents.md schema: channel, thread_ts, first_message_ts, last_message_ts, participants, and conversation in 'text'. All values are strings or list of strings.
